body.text: 'We should do something' tends to end in drinks. Drinks are lovely, but they're also loud, pricey, hard to talk over and an awkward fit for friends who aren't drinking, are driving, are saving or want to be home by ten.
Here are twenty-five alternatives, grouped by how much effort they take. Costs vary by city and group size, and the group sizes shown are suggestions rather than rules.
How to pick one for your group

items: **Ask two questions in the chat:** what's your budget, and do you want to talk or do something?
**Offer two options, not ten.** 'What does everyone want to do?' gets silence. 'Pottery or picnic?' gets answers.
**Pick the date first.** A plan with a date beats a plan with enthusiasm.
**Make it easy to say yes.** Under three hours, near transport.

**Ask about food needs.** Check for allergies and dietary requirements before you plan any snacks, and wash hands with soap and water before handling food; hand sanitizer doesn't remove food allergens.

body.title: Craft night
body.note: One simple craft, a big table, snacks. Everyone makes something a bit different and shows it off at the end. For a keepsake, [air-dry clay](/journal/how-to-start-air-dry-clay), [embroidery](/journal/how-to-start-embroidery) and [watercolor](/journal/watercolor-painting-for-beginners) all suit a table of friends. **What makes it easier:** a group painting kit or {{product:esrich-8x10-stretched-canvas-10-pack|a 10-pack of 8x10 canvases}} with acrylic paints, so everyone starts with the same thing in front of them. [How to host a paint night at home](/journal/how-to-host-a-paint-night-at-home) has the plan.

body.title: Cookie decorating party
body.note: Bake or buy plain cookies, set out icing and sprinkles and hold a very friendly contest. **What makes it easier:** a cookie decorating kit with icing and sprinkles, so the contest starts the moment the cookies cool.

body.title: Board game night
body.note: Choose a game you can explain in ten minutes, and keep a backup for whoever's knocked out first. **What makes it easier:** a party-size board game with simple rules, so the first round starts after one read-through.

body.title: Friendship-bracelet or bead night
body.note: Matching bracelets are quick, forgiving for beginners and lovely to hand over at the end. **What makes it easier:** a friendship bracelet kit, so the floss, beads and instructions arrive together. Check the label for small parts.

body.title: Mahjong night
body.note: Ideal if one friend already plays. Sets and rules differ by version, so agree which you're playing first; the [mahjong night guide](/journal/how-to-host-a-mahjong-night) covers how to start. **What makes it easier:** a set made for your version, a playing mat and the current reference card, so the first night starts with the game, not a hunt for pieces.

body.title: Movie marathon with a theme
body.note: Choose three films around a theme, like underrated rom-coms, and give each a matching snack. **What makes it easier:** a few big throws and flameless candles, so the living room turns into a cinema for the evening.

body.title: Puzzle and podcast evening
body.note: Tip a puzzle onto the table and let people drift in and out. Good for friends who don't want to perform. **What makes it easier:** a jigsaw puzzle sized for the table, so the edge pieces are sorted before the podcast starts.

body.title: Conversation-cards dinner
body.note: Draw a card between courses. Works well with friends you're sure you already know. **What makes it easier:** a deck of conversation cards, so there's a question ready between courses.

body.title: Vision-board and goals evening
body.note: Old magazines, scissors, glue sticks. Share one goal each and set a reminder to check in three months on. **What makes it easier:** card for the boards, scissors and {{product:scotch-glue-stick-photo-safe-4-pack|a glue stick}} each, so nobody waits for a turn with the glue.

body.title: Letter-writing night
body.note: Everyone writes postcards to people who aren't in the room. Bring stamps and good pens. **What makes it easier:** a letter-writing set or a pack of postcards and good pens, so everyone can start writing the moment they sit down.

body.title: Mocktail or tea tasting
body.note: Everyone brings an ingredient. Rank the results, crown a winner and ask about dietary needs beforehand. **What makes it easier:** a pot and a few mugs from a tea set, plus a tea sampler, so the tasting feels like an occasion.

body.title: Book club (one night only)
body.note: Read a short story or essay instead of a novel and talk it over. If it goes well, make it regular with [how to start a book club](/journal/how-to-start-a-book-club). **Worth bringing:** magnetic bookmarks and a small notebook each, so a favorite line is easy to mark and share.

body.text: The easiest hosting rule is one activity, one snack table and one end time. People relax when they know how the evening ends.

body.title: Start with a night-in kit
body.dek: A painting kit, a board game, a deck of conversation cards or a bracelet kit means "should we do something?" already has an answer.

body.title: For a mahjong night
body.dek: These picks are for American mahjong. Playing another version? Match the set and reference card to it, and check what the listing includes.

body.text: Out and about, with a bag packed

body.title: Farmers' market and picnic
body.note: Everyone buys one thing, then you assemble the lot on a blanket in a nearby park. **What makes it easier:** a picnic blanket and an insulated cooler bag, so the spread sits on one blanket and stays cold on the walk.

body.title: Beginner hike and snacks
body.note: Pick a popular, well-marked trail in daylight, tell someone your route, check the weather and pack water. Stay together as a group. **What makes it easier:** a daypack, a water bottle and walking shoes with grip, so snacks, water and a layer travel with you.

body.title: Pickleball or tennis on a public court
body.note: Many public courts are free or low cost, and beginner doubles is chatty and forgiving. Courts may have booking or time rules, so check locally. **What makes it easier:** a paddle set for four, so you don't depend on borrowed equipment; borrowing works too if a friend has spares.

body.title: Roller-skating night
body.note: Pure nostalgia. Everyone wobbles, which levels the field. Wear a helmet, wrist guards, and knee and elbow pads, and stay on the rink or a smooth paved surface in daylight. **What makes it easier:** a set of skate protective gear in your size, so the helmet, wrist guards and pads are ready before the night starts.

body.title: Thrift crawl with a challenge
body.note: Agree a spending cap and twenty minutes per shop each. Regroup, reveal your finds and vote. **Worth bringing:** a sturdy tote each, so finds ride on a shoulder and both hands stay free for the next rack.

body.title: For the outing nights
body.dek: A blanket, a daypack, a paddle set, skate pads and a tote each get a group out the door with everything in hand.

body.text: Getting the group chat to commit

items: Send one short message with two options, a date and a rough cost.
Give a deadline for replies, like 'let me know by Thursday'.
Be the one who books. Plans rarely survive committees.
Send a reminder two days before, and keep a smaller version of the plan for no-shows.

body.text: If craft night sounds like your group, start with [how to host a craft night](/journal/how-to-host-a-craft-night). Looking for a hobby of your own to start? See [15 hobbies to start this month](/journal/affordable-hobbies-under-25). For more ideas, browse [things to do after work instead of scrolling](/journal/things-to-do-after-work-instead-of-scrolling).
Free ways to start, and venue nights
Some of the easiest plans need no kit at all, or suit a studio or a venue better. Check hours, group sizes and booking rules ahead.

body.title: Pottery painting
body.note: Many studios let you paint a ready-made piece, then glaze and fire it for you. Group bookings vary, so check ahead. Prefer to stay in? See [how to host a paint night at home](/journal/how-to-host-a-paint-night-at-home).

body.title: Drop-in class
body.note: Dance, ceramics, life drawing, cooking: many studios offer a single session.

body.title: Museum with a coffee after
body.note: Choose one exhibit, then debrief over coffee.

body.title: Bookstore date with a book swap
body.note: Each friend picks a book for another within a budget cap, then everyone reads a first page aloud.

body.title: Walk-and-talk with a stop for treats
body.note: A loop around a park with a treat halfway. **Worth bringing:** an insulated flask of something warm to share.

body.title: Volunteer shift together
body.note: Many local groups welcome one-off volunteers. Check requirements and sign-ups ahead.

body.title: Dinner swap or potluck
body.note: Choose a theme, such as brunch for dinner, soup night or tacos, and have everyone bring one dish.

body.title: Spa night in
body.note: Face masks if you like them, foot soaks, a playlist. Follow product labels.

body.text: Think about who might be quietly left out. Choose a time that works around early mornings and childcare, a price nobody has to do sums over, and a place reachable without a car. If someone doesn't drink, don't build the plan around alcohol and don't ask why. Give people a graceful way to opt out of anything physical or messy. Rotating who chooses helps too, so nobody carries the planning alone.
Found one? Send this to the group chat and book the date before the thread goes quiet.
